title: The Sun only shines because particles tunnel through walls
body: Fusing hydrogen means forcing together protons that repel each other electrically. Even at about 15 million °C, protons in the Sun’s core almost never have enough energy to climb over that barrier. Quantum mechanics lets them occasionally “tunnel” straight through it instead, because a particle’s position is smeared out like a wave. Each tunnelling event is rare, but the core holds so many protons that it adds up to the Sun’s steady glow.

slides.question: Roughly how hot is the Sun’s core, in millions of degrees Celsius?
slides.explanation: About 15 million °C, yet protons there almost never have enough energy to climb over their electrical repulsion. They fuse because quantum mechanics lets them tunnel through the barrier.
